ports.name: clk_i
ports.functionality: Drives rising_edge sampling for PMP state elements. It times updates of pmpcfg, pmpaddr, addr_mask and the fault output so those registers change synchronously on clock edges.
ports.evidence: rising_edge(clk_i) branches in csr_pmpcfg, csr_pmpaddr, addr_masking and fault_check processes

ports.name: rstn_i
ports.functionality: Asynchronously or synchronously forces initial values for PMP registers. It resets pmpcfg, pmpaddr, addr_mask and fault_o in the processes' reset branches.
ports.evidence: if (rstn_i = '0') reset branches in csr_pmpcfg, csr_pmpaddr, addr_masking and fault_check processes

ports.name: ctrl_i
ports.functionality: Provides CSR addresses, enables, write data and access/control fields; its constituent fields drive CSR write enables, address selection, privilege selection and permission computation, and thereby influence internal PMP state and fault reporting.
ports.evidence: process headers and many RHS uses: csr_we_cfg, csr_we_addr, acc_addr/acc_priv assignments, perm_gen and fault_check processes (uses fields like csr_addr, csr_we, csr_wdata, lsu_mo_we, lsu_priv, lsu_rw, cpu_priv, cpu_debug)

ports.name: ctrl_i.lsu_mo_we

ports.name: ctrl_i.csr_we

ports.name: ctrl_i.csr_addr

ports.evidence: csr_we_cfg and csr_we_addr processes index write enables; csr_read_access uses ctrl_i.csr_addr to choose cfg_rd32 or addr_rd outputs

ports.name: ctrl_i.csr_wdata

ports.name: ctrl_i.cpu_debug
ports.functionality: Used to suppress fault reporting: the fault output samples (not ctrl_i.cpu_debug) AND fail(0) on clock edges, so cpu_debug effectively gates fault generation at the output.
ports.evidence: fault_check process: fault_o <= (not ctrl_i.cpu_debug) and fail(0) on rising_edge(clk_i)

ports.name: csr_o
ports.functionality: Drives CSR read result to the outside based on ctrl_i.csr_addr: it presents packed pmpcfg bytes (cfg_rd32) or read-back addresses (addr_rd) onto the bus.
ports.evidence: csr_read_access process assigns csr_o <= cfg_rd32(...) or addr_rd(...) based on ctrl_i.csr_addr

ports.name: addr_ls_i
ports.functionality: Supplies the load/store address used as acc_addr when lsu_mo_we = '1'; that chosen address is used for matching and permission checks.
ports.evidence: acc_addr <= ctrl_i.pc_nxt when (ctrl_i.lsu_mo_we = '0') else addr_ls_i

ports.name: fault_o
ports.functionality: Reports the sampled fault condition synchronous to clk: on clock edges it captures the combination of not cpu_debug AND fail(0), producing an external fault signal.
ports.evidence: fault_check process: on rising_edge(clk_i) fault_o <= (not ctrl_i.cpu_debug) and fail(0)

signals.name: pmpcfg
signals.functionality: Holds per-region 8-bit PMP configuration captured from CSR write data when write-enable is set; supplies these cfg bytes for readback, matching and permission logic.
signals.evidence: csr_pmpcfg process captures bits from ctrl_i.csr_wdata on rising_edge(clk_i); used by cfg_rd assignment, match_gen and perm_gen and gating pmpaddr writes

signals.name: pmpcfg_we
signals.functionality: Derived from CSR address and csr_we; it marks which pmpcfg byte-lane is being written and thus gates writes into pmpcfg registers.
signals.evidence: csr_we_cfg process sets pmpcfg_we based on ctrl_i.csr_addr(1 downto 0) and ctrl_i.csr_we

signals.name: pmpaddr
signals.functionality: Holds per-region PMP address values captured from CSR write data (with top bits padded); these addresses feed readback logic and form the basis for region comparisons.
signals.evidence: csr_pmpaddr process captures "00" & ctrl_i.csr_wdata(XLEN-3 downto 0) on rising_edge(clk_i); pmpaddr used in address_read_back, addr_mask_napot_gen and comparison expressions

signals.name: pmpaddr_we
signals.functionality: Derived from CSR address and csr_we; it selects which pmpaddr entry to write and thus gates pmpaddr register updates.
signals.evidence: csr_we_addr process sets pmpaddr_we based on ctrl_i.csr_addr(3 downto 0) and ctrl_i.csr_we

signals.name: cfg_rd
signals.functionality: Carries a direct copy of each pmpcfg entry for readback and packing; it is assigned the pmpcfg bytes and then aggregated into 32-bit words.
signals.evidence: cfg_rd(i) <= pmpcfg(i); cfg_rd32 packed from cfg_rd entries

signals.name: cfg_rd32
signals.functionality: Aggregates four cfg_rd bytes into a 32-bit word for CSR reads; these words drive csr_o when CSR read selects them.
signals.evidence: cfg_rd32(i) <= cfg_rd(i*4+3) & ... & cfg_rd(i*4+0); csr_read_access drives csr_o from cfg_rd32

signals.name: addr_rd
signals.functionality: Derived from pmpaddr and configuration bits (masks, TOR settings) to produce a canonical readback address; selected addr_rd entries drive csr_o for address CSR reads.
signals.evidence: address_read_back process assigns addr_rd(i) from pmpaddr(i) and pmpcfg(i); csr_read_access uses addr_rd(...) to drive csr_o

signals.name: acc_addr
signals.functionality: Combinationally selects the access address from ctrl_i.pc_nxt or addr_ls_i based on ctrl_i.lsu_mo_we; the chosen acc_addr is used for matching and comparison logic.
signals.evidence: acc_addr <= ctrl_i.pc_nxt when (ctrl_i.lsu_mo_we = '0') else addr_ls_i; cmp_ge/cmp_lt/cmp_na use acc_addr in their comparisons

signals.name: acc_priv
signals.functionality: Combinationally selects privilege from cpu_priv or lsu_priv (based on lsu_mo_we) and supplies it to the permission logic for allow(r) decisions.
signals.evidence: acc_priv <= ctrl_i.cpu_priv when (ctrl_i.lsu_mo_we = '0') else ctrl_i.lsu_priv; perm_gen uses acc_priv to compute allow(r)

signals.name: addr_mask_napot
signals.functionality: Combinationally builds the NPOT (NAPOT) match mask from pmpaddr bits for each region when NAP mode is enabled; the mask is a source for addr_mask assignment.
signals.evidence: addr_mask_napot_gen generate assigns bits from pmpaddr; addr_masking process assigns addr_mask(r) <= addr_mask_napot(r)

signals.name: addr_mask
signals.functionality: Registered per-region mask that is loaded from addr_mask_napot when al bit is set; it is used in the NAPOT comparison to determine matches.
signals.evidence: addr_masking clocked process captures addr_mask_napot into addr_mask when pmpcfg(r)(cfg_al_c) = '1'; cmp_na uses addr_mask(r)

signals.name: cmp_na
signals.functionality: Produces per-region 'NA' comparison results by comparing (acc_addr AND addr_mask) with (pmpaddr AND addr_mask) when NAP mode is enabled; its result is used to declare matches for NAPOT regions.
signals.evidence: cmp_na(r) <= '1' when ((acc_addr(...) and addr_mask(r)) = (pmpaddr(r)(...) and addr_mask(r))) and NAP_EN else '0'

signals.name: cmp_ge
signals.functionality: Per-region comparison indicating acc_addr >= pmpaddr(r-1) used for TOR region lower-bound testing when TOR is enabled; feeds match decision for TOR regions.
signals.evidence: cmp_ge(r) <= '1' when (unsigned(acc_addr(...)) >= unsigned(pmpaddr(r-1)(...))) and TOR_EN else '0'

signals.name: cmp_lt
signals.functionality: Per-region comparison indicating acc_addr < pmpaddr(r) used for TOR upper-bound testing when TOR is enabled; combined with cmp_ge to detect addresses inside TOR regions.
signals.evidence: cmp_lt(r) <= '1' when (unsigned(acc_addr(...)) < unsigned(pmpaddr(r)(...))) and TOR_EN else '0'

signals.name: match
signals.functionality: Per-region match result computed from pmpcfg mode and comparison signals (cmp_ge/cmp_lt for TOR, cmp_na for NAPOT); its asserted bits gate which region's permissions apply to an access.
signals.evidence: match_gen process sets match(r) from pmpcfg(...) and cmp_ge/cmp_lt/cmp_na

signals.name: allow
signals.functionality: Per-region permission bits computed from pmpcfg, acc_priv and the type of access (instruction/read/write as chosen by ctrl_i fields); an allow bit indicates the region permits execution/read/write for the current access.
signals.evidence: perm_gen process computes allow(r) via branches using pmpcfg(r) and acc_priv and tests ctrl_i.lsu_mo_we/ctrl_i.lsu_rw

signals.name: fail
signals.functionality: Reduction-style vector that produces a chained fault indication: fail(NUM_REGIONS) is set when acc_priv != machine, and for each region fail(r) becomes not allow(r) if that region matches, otherwise propagates the next fail. fail(0) drives fault output.
signals.evidence: fail(NUM_REGIONS) <= '1' when (acc_priv /= priv_mode_m_c) else '0'; fail(r) <= not allow(r) when (match(r) = '1') else fail(r+1); fault_check uses fail(0)
